title: Universal base change and tensor formula in the highest cohomological degree
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where $X,Y$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose $R^i h_*H=0$ for all $i>d$ and all quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $H$ [pqf-def-coherent, pqf-def-cohomology]. For any morphism $b:Y'\to Y$, form $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $b_X:X'\to X$ and $h':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then (a) $R^i h'_*H'=0$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X'}$-module $H'$ and $i>d$; (b) for every such $H'$ and quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{Y'}$-module $M'$, the canonical tensor projection map is an isomorphism $R^d h'_*H'\otimes_{\mathcal O_{Y'}}M'\xrightarrow{\sim}R^d h'_*(H'\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X'}}h'^*M')$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; (c) for every further morphism $c:Y''\to Y'$, with induced $c_X:X''=X'\times_{Y'}Y''\to X'$ and $h'':X''\to Y''$, the canonical degree-$d$ base-change map $c^*R^d h'_*H'\to R^d h''_*c_X^*H'$ is an isomorphism. Here all higher direct images concern structure-sheaf modules and all unadorned pullbacks are ordinary tensor pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, clauses (a)--(c), including the explanation of the canonical comparison in its proof.

proof.text: First $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and so are all its base changes, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. If $V\subset Y$ is affine, $U=h^{-1}V$ is a quasi-compact open in the quasi-separated scheme $X$. Its inclusion is quasi-compact. Given a quasi-coherent module $N$ on $U$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-extension-qc-open] with the ambient module zero and the map $N\to0$: it gives a quasi-coherent module on $X$ restricting to $N$. Higher-image open restriction [lem-pc-higher-direct-image-open-restriction] then transfers the assumed vanishing to $h|_U$. These same open-restriction identifications let us check all three conclusions on affine opens of $Y'$ and $Y''$ mapping into an affine open of $Y$. Hence in the calculations below the relevant bases are affine. The inverse images of those bases are qcqs, by the same permanence lemma. This is only a local reduction; $Y'$ and $Y''$ need not themselves be qcqs.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, reduction to affine bases

proof.text:
Assume $Y,Y'$ affine. The map $b$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], and $b_X$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. For quasi-coherent $H'$ the sheaf $b_{X,*}H'$ is quasi-coherent [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi]. For $i>d$, the affine cohomology edge [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] and the affine-base section comparison [lem-pc-affine-open-higher-direct-image-sections-iso] give
$$H^i(X',H')\cong H^i(X,b_{X,*}H')\cong\Gamma(Y,R^ih_*b_{X,*}H')=0.$$
Apply that section comparison to $h'$ as well: $\Gamma(Y',R^ih'_*H')=0$. The higher image is quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-ordinary-higher-image-quasi-coherent], so the affine tilde/global-section equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] makes it zero. This proves (a) locally and hence globally. It applies to every quasi-coherent $H'$, not just pullbacks from $X$.

For (b), put $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and fix $H'$. Define the $R$-linear functor $F(M)=H^d(X',E_M)$, where $E_M=H'\otimes h'^*\widetilde M$. The affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] describes the pulled module on each affine chart as extension of scalars; thus it is quasi-coherent. Tensor quasi-coherence follows from [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections]. The tilde functor preserves colimits [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], and tensor is right exact [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. Applying their affine formulas proves that an exact sequence $M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ gives $E_1\to E_2\to E_3\to0$ exact. Put $K=\ker(E_2\to E_3)$ and $L=\ker(E_1\to E_2)$; both are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. The two short exact sequences $0\to L\to E_1\to K\to0$ and $0\to K\to E_2\to E_3\to0$ give long exact cohomology sequences [pqf-def-cohomology]. By (a) and the affine-base section comparison, $H^{d+1}(X',L)=H^{d+1}(X',K)=0$. Consequently $H^d(E_1)\twoheadrightarrow H^d(K)$ and $H^d(K)\to H^d(E_2)\to H^d(E_3)\to0$ are exact. Their composite proves right exactness of $F$. Linearity is the functorial $R$-action on the cohomology of the section complex.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), right exactness

proof.text:
The three functors $M\mapsto\widetilde M$, $h'^*$, and $H'\otimes-$ preserve arbitrary direct sums: they are left adjoints, respectively by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], [def-pc-module-pullback] and [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Finally $H^d(X',-)$ commutes with direct sums because $X'$ is qcqs [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-cohomology-direct-sum]. Thus $F$ preserves arbitrary direct sums. Also $F(R)=H^d(X',H')$ by the tensor unit. Apply [lem-sfb-linear-right-exact-module-functor-tensor]: the isomorphism is the specified map
$$H^d(X',H')\otimes_RM\longrightarrow H^d(X',H'\otimes h'^*\widetilde M),\qquad x\otimes m\longmapsto H^d(H'\xrightarrow{\,s\mapsto s\otimes h'^*m\,}E_M)(x).$$
This is the canonical tensor projection map on affine-base sections, since its restriction at each $m:R\to M$ is that cohomology map. Both higher images are quasi-coherent [lem-pc-ordinary-higher-image-quasi-coherent]. The cocycle class maps $H^d(X',-)\to\Gamma(Y',R^dh'_*-)$ on quasi-coherent modules are bijective over the affine $Y'$ [lem-pc-affine-resolution-section-bijective], and they commute with the map induced by a module morphism, since it carries cocycles of a resolution to cocycles of a resolution. With the affine tensor-section formula [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] they identify the displayed map with the sections over $Y'$ of the canonical map of (b), which on a local section $m$ of $\widetilde M$ is $R^dh'_*$ of $s\mapsto s\otimes h'^*m$. The tilde/global-section equivalence detects its invertibility. This proves (b) locally and hence globally.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (b), sums and the module-functor exercise

proof.text:
For (c) work over $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Y''=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and put $p=c_X$. There is an isomorphism
$$p_*p^*H'\cong H'\otimes h'^*\widetilde B.$$
Indeed, on an affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X'$ with $H'|_W=\widetilde N$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso] identifies the inverse image with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RB)$. The affine pullback formula identifies the left-hand module with $N\otimes_A(A\otimes_RB)$ and the right-hand module with $N\otimes_A(A\otimes_RB)$ by the affine tensor-section formula. Both identifications send the pullback unit of $n$ to $n\otimes1$; their formulas commute with ring restriction and hence glue. The cited affine tilde equivalence identifies the sheaves from these modules. No flatness is used.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (c), affine-chart push-pull calculation

proof.text:
Since $p$ is affine, its cohomology edge gives
$$H^d(X'',p^*H')\cong H^d(X',p_*p^*H')\cong H^d(X',H'\otimes h'^*\widetilde B)\cong H^d(X',H')\otimes_R B.$$
The last arrow is the inverse of (b); the first is the inverse edge isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge]. Under these identifications the map in the forward direction sends $x\otimes b$ to $b$ times the cohomological pullback of $x$ along the unit $H'\to p_*p^*H'$. This follows from the normalization in the preceding step and the formula for (b): at $b=1$ it is the cohomology of that unit followed by the affine edge; $B$-linearity gives general $b$. Thus the ordinary cohomological unit comparison is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, proof of (c), final cohomology calculation

proof.text: We identify the canonical map of (c). Put $C=Rh'_*(H'[0])$; by (a) it has cohomology zero above $d$, and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-pullback-top-cohomology] gives $\kappa_{c,C}:H^d(Lc^*C)\xrightarrow{\sim}c^*R^dh'_*H'$. Let $\delta_c:Lc^*C\to Rh''_*((p^*H')[0])$ be the canonical module base-change map: the derived base-change map [def-pc-derived-base-change-map] followed by the derived-to-ordinary pullback comparison on $H'$ [def-pc-derived-module-base-change-map]. The map of (c), as in the source, is $\gamma=H^d(\delta_c)\kappa_{c,C}^{-1}:c^*R^dh'_*H'\to R^dh''_*p^*H'$. Let $a:R^dh'_*H'\to c_*R^dh''_*p^*H'$ be its ordinary adjoint [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], so $a(s)=\gamma(c^*s)$ on sections. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-top-base-change-presheaf] with $f=h'$, $F=H'$, $q=d$, $g=c$ and $V=Y'$; then $U=X'$, $W=Y''$, $U'=X''$ and $v_V=p$. It gives $\Gamma(Y',a)\theta_{Y'}=\theta'_{Y''}p^*$, where $p^*$ is the cohomology map of the pullback unit $H'\to p_*p^*H'$. As $h',h''$ are qcqs (step 1), $H'$ and $p^*H'$ are quasi-coherent and $Y',Y''$ are affine, both cocycle class maps $\theta_{Y'}:H^d(X',H')\to\Gamma(Y',R^dh'_*H')$ and $\theta'_{Y''}:H^d(X'',p^*H')\to\Gamma(Y'',R^dh''_*p^*H')$ are bijective [lem-pc-affine-resolution-section-bijective].

source.place: Tag 0EX3, lemma-top-cohomology-functor, explanation of the canonical map before the proof and final paragraph

proof.text: Since $R^dh'_*H'$ is quasi-coherent [lem-pc-ordinary-higher-image-quasi-coherent], the affine pullback formula [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] gives $\Gamma(Y'',c^*R^dh'_*H')\cong\Gamma(Y',R^dh'_*H')\otimes_RB$, $s\otimes b\mapsto b\,c^*s$. By $B$-linearity and step 7, $\Gamma(Y'',\gamma)(s\otimes b)=b\,\Gamma(Y',a)(s)$. Through the bijections $\theta_{Y'}$ and $\theta'_{Y''}$ of step 7 this is the map $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,p^*x$ from $H^d(X',H')\otimes_RB$ to $H^d(X'',p^*H')$, proved invertible in step 6. Source and target of $\gamma$ are quasi-coherent, by the affine pullback formula and [lem-pc-ordinary-higher-image-quasi-coherent]. The affine tilde/global-section equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] therefore makes $\gamma$ an isomorphism over $Y''$. The base-change construction restricts to opens [def-pc-derived-base-change-map], and open restriction of higher images [lem-pc-higher-direct-image-open-restriction] then proves (c) for arbitrary $c$.
